items.says: Standard Diebold-Mariano inference does not validly confirm a forecast gain in a nested-model comparison.
items.because: Standard DM tests can have incorrect size for nested forecasts, and testing 30 indices requires accounting for multiple comparisons.

items.says: The line does not give the size of the forecast gain or the outcome of the tests.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the claimed advantage from the test name and index count alone.

items.says: The opening participial phrase dangles instead of clearly connecting the feature-joining actions to building the store.
items.because: “Joining” appears to modify an unstated actor, while “built” introduces a different subject.

items.says: The reuse outcome comes after several implementation details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the clearest evidence of the feature store’s value.

items.says: Multiplying the daily Sharpe ratio by 252 does not correctly annualize it.
items.because: The usual scaling is √252 for sufficiently uncorrelated daily returns; serial correlation requires a different adjustment.

items.says: The feature-store, annualization, and onboarding details pull attention from the internship’s signal and trading-cost results.
items.because: Those bullets branch away from the internship’s research narrative.

items.says: “The previous bound” does not identify the comparator or setting for the log-factor improvement.
items.because: Without that context, a reader cannot assess the contribution’s significance.

items.says: The package, cluster, teaching, and course duties read as a mixed task list.
items.because: The duties separate the package’s adoption evidence from its release and risk overshadowing the strongest research contribution.

items.says: The stated 33% improvement is wrong; the decrease from 0.20 to 0.15 is 25%.
items.because: The decrease of 0.05 is 25% of the original 0.20.

items.says: The line does not name the forecast-error metric or say what the 0.20 value represents.
items.because: Without the metric and comparison context, a reader cannot interpret the values or tell what changed.

items.says: The hit rate rose by 6 percentage points, not 6% relative to its original value.
items.because: The increase from 52% to 58% is about 11.5% relative to the original rate.

items.says: The temporal convolutional model detail repeats information from the first bullet.
items.because: Repeating the model type takes space without distinguishing the contribution.

items.says: “Finishing in the top 2%” repeats the rank of 41st out of 2,900.
items.because: The rank already communicates the placement.

items.says: The gap closing does not establish that validation leakage was reduced or that the fold change caused the closure.
items.because: Other leakage paths may remain, and the gap can change because of sampling variation, distribution shift, or evaluation differences.
The misspelling can distract a reader from the skills.
